topic: Pension income splitting: a pensioner may elect jointly with a spouse/common-law partner to report up to 50% of eligible pension income on the partner's return (Form T1032), every year; CPP/OAS excluded; under 65 only life annuity from a pension plan qualifies (RRIF only at 65+ or on a spouse's death)

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Manitoba couple, both 66 at the end of 2026; Pat: $80,000 registered pension plan life pension + $20,000 CPP/OAS; Jo: $20,000 CPP/OAS. Bracket tax on 2026 federal + Manitoba rates; the basic personal amount is claimed either way and cancels; Jo's new pension credit = federal $2,000 x 14% + Manitoba $1,000 x 10.8%. Not modelled: age amount, OAS recovery tax, withholding. Computed by r5/calc.py.

sources.split: ITA 60.03(1) 'split-pension amount' = up to 0.5 x eligible pension income (pro-rated by months married); 'joint election' in prescribed form filed with both returns by their filing-due dates; laws-lois.justice.gc.ca (fetched 2026-10-24)
sources.effect: ITA 60.03(2): the transferee is deemed to receive the split amount as pension income / qualified pension income for s. 118(3); 56(1)(a.2) and 60(c) include/deduct it
sources.eligible: ITA 118(7): at 65+ pension income incl. RRIF payments and RRSP annuity; under 65 'qualified pension income' = life annuity from a superannuation or pension plan, or the other items only as a consequence of the death of a spouse
sources.excluded: ITA 118(8)(a)-(b): OAS and CPP/QPP benefits are not pension income
sources.credit: ITA 118(3): credit on the lesser of $2,000 and eligible pension income x appropriate percentage (14% for 2026); Manitoba pension amount $1,000 (gov.mb.ca Personal Tax Credits, fetched 2026-10-24) x 10.8%
sources.form: Form T1032, Joint Election to Split Pension Income: both spouses file it with their returns by the filing due date; one joint election per tax year (canada.ca 'Pension income splitting', CRA; found via search 2026-10-24); transferor deducts on line 21000, transferee reports on line 11600
